visualConcepts.title: Firm Financial Health: Net Multiplier, Overhead & Utilization
visualConcepts.subtitle: Amber Book & Hyperfine Visual Formula Breakdown
visualConcepts.keyFormula: Net Multiplier = Net Operating Revenue / Direct Labor  |  Break-Even = 1 + (Overhead / Direct Labor)
takeaways: Net Operating Revenue (NOR) = Gross Revenue minus outside consultant pass-throughs and reimbursable expenses.
Utilization Rate = Direct Billable Hours / Total Hours Paid (Firm target: 60–65%; Technical staff target: 75–85%).
If Net Multiplier > Break-Even Rate, the firm is profitable. Typical healthy architecture firm Net Multiplier is 3.0 to 3.3.

visualConcepts.title: AIA Contract Relationships Matrix (DBB, CMAR, DB, IPD)
visualConcepts.subtitle: Who Contracts With Whom & How Communications Flow
takeaways: In Design-Bid-Build (A201), the Architect has NO direct contract with the Contractor or Subcontractors.
All communications with Subcontractors must go through the General Contractor; all communications with Consultants go through the Architect.
Only the Owner can stop the Work (A201 Sec. 2.4); the Architect can REJECT non-conforming Work (Sec. 4.2.6).

visualConcepts.title: Zoning FAR vs. Setbacks & Buildable Envelope
visualConcepts.subtitle: Walking the ARE #1 Trap to Avoid on Test Day
visualConcepts.keyFormula: Max Gross Floor Area (GFA) = FAR × Total Lot Area (NEVER multiply FAR by Setback Area!)
takeaways: Floor Area Ratio (FAR) always multiplies against the ENTIRE legal lot area, before subtracting setbacks.
Setbacks and Maximum Lot Coverage (%) determine the maximum single-floor footprint.
Minimum Number of Stories Required = Max GFA / Max Single-Floor Footprint.

visualConcepts.title: HVAC System Selection & Acoustic/Energy Trade-Offs
visualConcepts.subtitle: VAV vs. CAV vs. DOAS + Chilled Beams vs. VRF
visualConcepts.keyFormula: Sensible Heat: Q = 1.08 × CFM × ΔT  |  Sabine Reverberation: RT60 = 0.049 × V / A
takeaways: Large Assembly / Auditorium: Single-zone Constant Air Volume (CAV) with low air velocity for acoustic quietness.
Multi-zone Office / Classroom: Variable Air Volume (VAV) with terminal reheat or VRF heat recovery.
Low Floor-to-Floor Renovation: Hydronic (water pipes take 80% less plenum depth than all-air ductwork) or VRF.

visualConcepts.title: The 4 Barrier Layers in Exterior Wall Assemblies
visualConcepts.subtitle: Water, Air, Thermal, and Vapor Control (In Order of Importance)
visualConcepts.keyFormula: Vapor Retarder Rule: Always install on the WARM-IN-WINTER side of the insulation!
takeaways: 1. Water-Resistive Barrier (WRB) + Flashing + Weep Holes + Air Cavity (drains liquid bulk water outward).
2. Continuous Air Barrier (prevents air leakage carrying 100x more moisture than vapor diffusion).
3. Continuous Exterior Insulation (keeps structural studs warm above the condensation dew point).
4. Vapor Retarder: Interior side of studs in Cold climates (Zones 5–8); Exterior side in Hot-Humid climates (Zones 1–2).

visualConcepts.title: Construction Administration Document Authority (ASI vs. CCD vs. CO)
visualConcepts.subtitle: When Cost & Time Change During Construction
visualConcepts.keyFormula: ASI (G710) = 1 Sig (Arch)  |  CCD (G714) = 2 Sigs (Owner+Arch)  |  CO (G701) = 3 Sigs (Owner+Arch+GC)
takeaways: Before Bid Opening: Use written Addenda (AIA A701) to modify bidding documents.
After Contract Execution: Minor change with NO cost/time impact = ASI (G710, signed by Architect only).
Disputed price/time where work must proceed immediately = CCD (G714, signed by Owner & Architect).
Agreed price/time adjustment = Change Order (G701, signed by Owner, Architect, AND Contractor).

flashcards.front: What is the formula for Net Multiplier, and what benchmark indicates a healthy architectural firm?
flashcards.back: Net Multiplier = Net Operating Revenue (NOR) / Direct Salary Expense (DSE). A healthy firm targets 3.0 to 3.3+ (must exceed the Break-Even Rate = 1 + Overhead Rate).

flashcards.front: How does a 'Claims-Made' Professional Liability Insurance policy work if a claim is filed 4 years after construction?
flashcards.back: The coverage limits and deductible in effect AT THE TIME THE CLAIM IS FILED govern (not when the building was designed), provided continuous retroactive 'tail' coverage was maintained.

flashcards.front: Under AIA B101-2017 Section 6.7, what is the Architect's obligation if the lowest bid exceeds the Owner's budget for the Cost of the Work?
flashcards.back: If the Owner elects to revise project scope/quality, the Architect must modify the Construction Documents WITHOUT additional compensation to comply with the budget.

flashcards.front: Which AIA contract links the Architect and Structural/MEP Consultants, and how does payment timing work?
flashcards.back: AIA C401-2017. It uses a 'pay-when-paid' provision: the Architect pays the Consultant promptly after receiving payment from the Owner (unless nonpayment is due to the Architect's fault).

flashcards.front: Under IBC Section 303.1.2, how is a lecture room or conference room under 750 SF (or <50 occupants) classified inside an office building?
flashcards.back: It is classified as Group B (Business) or part of the main occupancy, rather than triggering a separate Group A (Assembly) occupancy classification.

flashcards.front: On a topographic map, do contour V-shapes pointing UPHILL represent a valley/swale or a ridge?
flashcards.back: Contour lines pointing UPHILL (toward higher elevations) always indicate a valley, swale, or drainage channel; contours pointing DOWNHILL indicate a ridge or nose.

flashcards.front: Under IBC Chapter 10, what is the minimum separation distance between two required exits in a non-sprinklered vs. fully sprinklered (NFPA 13) building?
flashcards.back: Non-sprinklered: >= 1/2 the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the building/area served. Fully sprinklered (NFPA 13): >= 1/3 the maximum overall diagonal dimension.

flashcards.front: When should you specify a Pre-Action fire sprinkler system instead of a Wet-Pipe or Dry-Pipe system?
flashcards.back: In water-sensitive spaces (museums, rare book libraries, server rooms). Pre-Action requires BOTH a smoke/heat detector trigger AND a fused sprinkler head before water discharges.

flashcards.front: Where should the Vapor Retarder be placed in an insulated wall assembly in Chicago/Minneapolis (ASHRAE Zone 5A/6A)?
flashcards.back: On the WARM-IN-WINTER side of the insulation (the interior face of the studs just behind the interior drywall), preventing warm indoor moisture from condensing in the cold wall cavity.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between CSI MasterFormat Division 00 and Division 01?
flashcards.back: Division 00 (Procurement & Contracting Requirements: Bid info, A101, A201) is NOT part of the Specifications. Division 01 (General Requirements: Submittals, Allowances, Closeout) is the first division of the Specifications and governs Divisions 02–49.

flashcards.front: What are the 4 sequential steps of Project Closeout from Contractor notice to final payment under AIA A201?
flashcards.back: 1. Contractor submits punch list & requests inspection -> 2. Architect inspects & issues Certificate of Substantial Completion (G704) -> 3. Contractor completes punch list & submits closeout docs (G706, G706A, G707) -> 4. Architect conducts final inspection & issues Final Certificate for Payment.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between Sick Building Syndrome (SBS) and Building-Related Illness (BRI)?
flashcards.back: SBS causes acute discomfort (headaches, eye irritation from VOCs/poor ventilation) that disappears shortly after leaving the building. BRI (e.g., Legionnaires' disease) has a clinically diagnosable pathogen and symptoms persist after leaving.
